messages:
maria (PM): Kicking off PRD intake for structured-output validation on Redwood API. Problem: customers (fintech / healthcare) need deterministic JSON shapes from generation endpoints so downstream pipelines don't break. We've seen a few P1s from bad schema drift.
kevin (Eng): quick q — do we want strict schema enforcement server-side or a best-effort sanitized output + warnings? Those are very different infra tradeoffs.
sasha (Research): Problem clarifying: model hallucination of field names and types is the main source of failures. We can combine prompt engineering + lightweight post-parse validation.
aj (Design): Goals I care about: 1) clear SDK flags so apps can opt into structured mode, 2) minimal changes to existing UX, 3) sample error surfaces for devs. Non-goal: not building a full-on user-facing schema editor in V1.
kevin (Eng): Proposal (V1): accept a user-supplied JSON Schema (draft-07 subset) or simple field spec; run output through server-side sanitizer that attempts to coerce types and fill missing keys. If coercion fails, return a structured error object and a stable fallback (raw string with trace-id).
sasha (Research): Acceptance criteria idea: - Valid-schema percentage >= 99.9% on our internal prompt set - End-to-end ingestion failures caused by schema mismatch < 0.1% for customers who enable feature - No more than +15% median latency for small payloads
kevin (Eng): Example response formats (proto):
```json
Success: { "ok": true, "data": { /* normalized object matching schema */ }, "meta": {"schema_version": "v1", "sanitized": true} }
Error: { "ok": false, "error": "schema_mismatch", "details": {"missing_keys": ["amount"], "coercions": {"date": "coerced"}, "trace_id": "abcd"} }
```
aj (Design): Edge cases to call out: - partial matches where only some fields are wrong - arrays with mixed-type elements - very large nested objects (limit depth?) Also want examples in the SDK docs for common patterns.
devex-bot: Checklist created: https://redwood.example.org/prd-checks/structured-output (owner required: maria). :white_check_mark:
zach (SRE): Rollout plan must support safe fallback. Suggest canary: 1% for 24h -> 10% 48h -> 100%. Expose metrics: schema_mismatch_rate, sanitize_time_p50/p95, user_fallback_rate. Also rate-limit validation to avoid DoS amplification.
maria (PM): Success metrics (proposal): 1) schema_mismatch_rate <= 0.1% for enabled customers within 30 days 2) developer adoption: 10 customers on dedicated beta in 60 days 3) no more than 2 incident pages caused by this feature in first 90 days.
kevin (Eng): Implementation notes: prefer async validation pipeline if possible. For hosted API we can do sync sanitize for small responses (<2KB). For bigger payloads route to background job + webhook. Need API param: `structured_schema` (string or s3 ref) + `structured_mode`: [strict|sanitize|warn].
sasha (Research): Eval plan: build prompt templates + fuzzing harness to surface common hallucinations and measure sanitize success. We'll prepare 1k sample prompts per vertical (fintech, healthcare, e-comm).
aj (Design): Acceptance criteria for docs: quickstart + 3 examples (payments, patient-record, product-catalog) and a troubleshooting section with sample errors and fixes.
maria (PM): Non-goals recap: not replacing customer-side validation; not supporting arbitrary user-defined code execution; no UI schema editor in V1.
maria (PM): Next steps: I'll spin up an RFC draft (owner: maria) with sections: problem, goals/non-goals, success metrics, rollout, API design, acceptance criteria, eval plan, infra impact. Kevin and Sasha please add tech/ops estimates. Can we aim to have RFC ready for review by EOW? :calendar:
kevin (Eng): EOW is tight but doable for an MVP RFC. I'll add rough estimates and a minimal API spec.
sasha (Research): I'll upload the initial eval harness and first 300 prompts by tomorrow.
aj (Design): I'll prototype SDK experience and example snippets by mid-week.
maria (PM): Thanks — tagging @product-review for RFC cycle when ready. :eyes:
